title: Build a max-priority queue in Go using container/heap
description: Greenfield Go task: implement a string priority queue that always pops the highest-priority item. Uses container/heap internally.

task_spec.prompt:
Create internal/pqueue/pqueue.go implementing a max-priority queue (highest priority pops first).

Required types and functions:

  type Item struct {
      Value    string
      Priority int
  }

  type PQueue struct { ... }  // internal representation using container/heap

  func New() *PQueue
  func (pq *PQueue) Push(value string, priority int)
  func (pq *PQueue) Pop() (Item, bool)   // returns (zero, false) when empty
  func (pq *PQueue) Peek() (Item, bool)  // inspect highest-priority without removing
  func (pq *PQueue) Len() int
  func (pq *PQueue) IsEmpty() bool

Use container/heap from the standard library for the heap operations.

All 5 tests in internal/pqueue/pqueue_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Item struct with Value string and Priority int
Peek does not remove the item
IsEmpty/Len are consistent with pushes and pops
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
